subject: Runtime rebrand & integration — contractual and technical roadmap
messages:
From: Jane Park <jane.park@edgeware.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Paul Reynolds <paul@northbridge.co>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: White-label runtime opportunity — EdgeWare x Redwood

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week. EdgeWare leadership is excited about the prospect of incorporating Redwood's runtime into our Portal product under a white-label arrangement (we'd surface it as the "EdgeWare Assist" runtime).

High-level asks from our side:
- Commercial: one-year exclusive pilot for Portal customers in the financial vertical; we'd like pricing bands and an MRR-friendly SKU.
- Technical: a relocatable runtime package and a minimal rebrand surface (logo + minor UI text). We need an offline installer for on-prem customers.
- Legal: a simple co-branding framework and IP clarity for derived prompts/templates.

Can you share a short commercial and tech checklist we can use to scope internal approval? Paul from our systems integrator is looped for deployment questions — he can provide our standard SOW template.

Appreciate it,
Jane
VP Partnerships, EdgeWare
[EdgeWare logo]

[Attachment: EW_branding_guidelines_v1.docx (docx, 92KB)]

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Jane Park <jane.park@edgeware.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: White-label runtime opportunity — EdgeWare x Redwood

Hi Jane — great to hear. Short answers below and a proposal for next steps: 

Quick commercial outline (high-level):
- Pilot term: 12 months, non-exclusive by default but options for exclusivity on specific segments (financial vertical) with minimum commitment.
- Pricing: base reserved capacity + per-token overage for hosted routes; for on-prem/offline a licensing + support fee (we can provide a pricing matrix).
- SKUs: Portal-Hosted, Portal-Dedicated, Portal-Private (on-prem installer).

Technical checklist (summary):
- Relocatable runtime artifact: yes (installer + Docker).
- Rebrand surface: logo, color token swap, product name; localization support for UI strings.
- Security: KMS integration for keys, audit logs export, SOC2 options.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Discovery call w/ product & infra (30–45m) this week — Karthik and our infra lead will join to map integration points.
2) Exchange SOW and a short co-branding appendix (we can draft).
3) Quick compatibility checklist from our side for on-prem customers.

I'm attaching a starter SOW + a runtime compatibility checklist you can pass to Paul.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Strategic Partner Manager | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Hi Rachel — thanks. Attaching our SOW template and the brand appendix. A couple of points from our side that we'll need addressed in the draft SOW: 

1) On-prem distribution: the installer must support an air-gapped deployment path and provide automated KV-seal/unseal instructions (we typically require these for financial customers).
2) Derived IP: we want clarity that EdgeWare retains ownership of customer-facing templates and prompt sets we build together; Redwood retains runtime code and model IP.
3) Support SLAs: for pilot customers we need 24x5 support with a defined escalation path to Redwood infra on call.

I've asked Paul to add a technical appendix about how our integrator will run the initial deployment.

Thanks,
Jane

Folks — technical delta summary (first-pass):
- On-prem/air-gapped installer: we can provide an OCI bundle + an offline key provisioning sequence. Estimated engineering effort: 3–4 sprints (infra + packaging).
- Branding surface: trivial for runtime; for the Portal UI we'll expose a config file and a small SDK hook for color/logo. Estimate: 1 sprint for SDK hook + 1 sprint for docs.
- Compliance & audit logs: SOC2 necessary; pushing for log export endpoints and retention settings in SOW.

Action items to include in SOW:
- Deliverables: installer artifact, branding guide integration doc, runbook for KMS and audit log export.
- Timeline: pilot MVP in 10 weeks from contract signature.
- Escalation: include on-call contact and response SLAs (24x5).

I'll draft a short technical appendix that Rachel can attach to the commercial SOW. Marissa — let's coordinate onboarding resources if this moves to pilot.

—Karthik
Product Lead, Integrations | Redwood Inference

From: legal@edgeware.ai <legal@edgeware.ai>

Cc: Jane Park <jane.park@edgeware.ai>, Paul Reynolds <paul@northbridge.co>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 12:05:00 -08:00
Subject: EdgeWare — proposed IP/branding language (redlines)

Rachel,

Thanks for sending the starter SOW. We have three redlines in the co-brand appendix: 
1) Wording that makes explicit EdgeWare ownership of customer-configured templates and any derivative prompt libraries created under this program.
2) A carve-out that allows EdgeWare to use the rebranded runtime name in marketing materials and customer-facing docs with a co-review step.
3) A limitation on transfer of customer data to Redwood-hosted environments without prior written consent (important for regulated clients).

We're open to reasonable language that protects Redwood's runtime IP while preserving EdgeWare's ability to commercialize the co-branded product. If you can share a proposed legal appendix, we can iterate.

Regards,
EdgeWare Legal
